title: The free-module complex of the Cech nerve of a surjection of sets resolves the free module on the target
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a surjective map of sets and $R$ a ring. For $n\geq0$ let $A_n=A\times_B\cdots\times_BA$ ($n+1$ factors) $=\{(a_0,\dots,a_n)\in A^{n+1}:f(a_0)=\cdots=f(a_n)\}$, with face maps $d_j:A_n\to A_{n-1}$ omitting the $j$-th coordinate, and let $R[A_n]$ be the free $R$-module on $A_n$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $\partial=\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jR[d_j]:R[A_n]\to R[A_{n-1}]$ and $\varepsilon=R[f]:R[A_0]=R[A]\to R[B]$, $[a]\mapsto[f(a)]$. Then $\partial\circ\partial=0$, $\varepsilon\circ\partial=0$, and the augmented complex $\cdots\to R[A_2]\to R[A_1]\to R[A_0]\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}R[B]\to0$ is exact; in particular $H_i(R[A_\bullet],\partial)=0$ for $i>0$ and $\varepsilon$ induces $H_0(R[A_\bullet])\cong R[B]$. (Concretely, for a chosen section $\sigma:B\to A$ of $f$, the maps $[(a_0,\dots,a_n)]\mapsto[(\sigma f(a_0),a_0,\dots,a_n)]$ and $[b]\mapsto[\sigma(b)]$ form a contracting homotopy of the augmented complex.)

proof.text: Surjectivity of $f$ lets us choose one $\sigma(b)\in f^{-1}(b)$ for every $b\in B$; thus $f\sigma=\operatorname{id}_B$. Define $R$-linear maps on the free-module bases [def-weil-pbc-free-module] by $h_{-1}[b]=[\sigma(b)]$ and, for $n\geq0$, $h_n[(a_0,\ldots,a_n)]=[(\sigma f(a_0),a_0,\ldots,a_n)]$. All coordinates of the latter tuple have the same $f$-image, so $h_n$ lands in $R[A_{n+1}]$. The empty-set case is included: a surjection $A\to\varnothing$ forces $A=\varnothing$, and the zero maps give the same formulas. Lean implementation: prepend and homotopy construct these maps explicitly; vertex and sectionMap construct the augmentation section. The right inverse is obtained from the proved theorem Function.Surjective.hasRightInverse.

proof.text: For $i<j$, deleting coordinate $j$ and then $i$ gives the same tuple as deleting $i$ and then $j-1$. In $\partial^2$, these two terms have coefficients $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and cancel; hence $\partial^2=0$. In degree one, $\varepsilon\partial[(a_0,a_1)]=[f(a_1)]-[f(a_0)]=0$, since $(a_0,a_1)\in A_1$; this is $\varepsilon\partial=0$. Lean implementation: face_face proves the deletion identity coordinatewise. differential_squared partitions the double sum into j ≤ i and its complement and pairs (i,j) with (j,i+1), following the finite-sum argument of Mathlib AlternatingFaceMapComplex.d_squared. augmentation_differential proves the degree-one identity on basis vectors.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemmas Tags 03AS and 03AT (labels lemma-cech-map-into and lemma-homology-complex), alternating-face complex

proof.text: On a basis tuple $x=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $n\geq1$, the zeroth face of $h_n(x)$ is $x$. For $1\leq j\leq n+1$, its $j$th face is the prefixed tuple obtained by deleting $a_{j-1}$ from $x$; when $j=1$, its prefix is still $\sigma f(a_0)$ because all entries of $x$ have the same image in $B$. Thus the remaining terms of $\partial h_n(x)$ cancel term by term against $h_{n-1}\partial(x)$, giving $\partial h_n+h_{n-1}\partial=\operatorname{id}_{R[A_n]}$. For $n=0$, the two faces of $h_0[a]$ give $\partial h_0[a]=[a]-[\sigma f(a)]$, while $h_{-1}\varepsilon[a]=[\sigma f(a)]$. Finally $\varepsilon h_{-1}[b]=[f\sigma(b)]=[b]$. Linearity extends all three identities from basis elements to modules. Lean implementation: face_prepend_zero and face_prepend_succ identify the faces; homotopy_identity, homotopy_identity_zero, and augmentation_section prove the three linear-map identities by free-module extensionality.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 03AT (label lemma-homology-complex), final paragraph, prefixing homotopy; Stacks 01GC applies this fibrewise to the nerve

proof.text: For $n>0$ and $z\in\ker\partial\subseteq R[A_n]$, step 3 gives $z=\partial h_n(z)$, so $H_n=0$. In degree zero, a $z$ with $\varepsilon(z)=0$ satisfies $z=\partial h_0(z)$, and step 2 gives the reverse inclusion $\operatorname{im}\partial\subseteq\ker\varepsilon$. Since $\varepsilon h_{-1}=\operatorname{id}$, the augmentation is onto; consequently $R[A_0]/\operatorname{im}\partial\cong R[B]$, with the stated map on $H_0$. Together with step 2 these equalities prove exactness at every term, including $R[B]$. Lean implementation: range_eq_ker_of_contraction proves both inclusions, sending a cycle z to its explicit preimage h(z). The final theorem applies this in degree zero and in every positive degree, and uses augmentation_section to prove surjectivity.
